verified.exploit_entry_point: The plugin management operations of pkg/plugin.Manager, reached from the `trivy plugin` CLI subcommands (install, uninstall, info, repair, update) and from the package's public Go API. The hidden tests drive the real Manager methods (NewManager().Install/Uninstall/Information/Start/Repair/Update) with XDG_DATA_HOME pointed at a temp directory and, for the index route, WithIndexURL pointed at a local file-URL mirror; nothing is stubbed. The attacker input is a plugin name carried in a plugin's packaged metadata, in the metadata stored on disk from an earlier install, in a plugin-index entry, or in a command-line argument.
variants: base (published fix, pattern A): a plugin's packaged metadata declares a name such as '../escaped_plugin', 'missing/../../escaped_clean' or '../plugins_evil'; the install destination is the name joined onto the plugin directory, so the downloader clears and writes outside the plugin directory and the metadata copy is written outside it.

symlink shape (published fix, pattern A): the packaged name is a valid relative path ('link/sub') whose parent inside the plugin directory is an existing symlink that points outside; the joined destination is cleared and written through the link.

far command-line site (published fix, pattern A): Uninstall joins its argument onto the plugin directory and removes it, and Information loads metadata through the same join; a '..'-bearing or bare '..' argument reaches outside.

stored-name site (published fix, pattern A): loadMetadata derives the plugin's directory from the name recorded in the metadata on disk, so an installed plugin whose stored name escapes makes a later Start execute a program outside the plugin directory and makes the injected Repair rewrite metadata outside it.

injected sibling (index cache): a plugin-index entry's name is joined onto the plugin directory when Update writes a per-plugin index cache; a hostile entry name in a mirrored index creates a directory outside the plugin directory.
sites: pkg/plugin/manager.go:333-359 (loadMetadata derives plugin.dir from the stored name)
pkg/plugin/plugin.go:69 (exec path joins Platform.Bin onto the stored-name-derived directory)
routes: CLI `trivy plugin install <src>` and the public Install method
CLI `trivy plugin uninstall <name>` and the public Uninstall method
CLI `trivy plugin info <name>` and the public Information method
CLI `trivy plugin run <name>` / output-plugin Start and the public Start method
CLI `trivy plugin update` and the public Update method (custom index URL via WithIndexURL)
CLI `trivy plugin repair` and the public Repair method
verified.project_tests_run: The project's own pkg/plugin suite (manager_test.go, manager_unix_test.go, index_test.go) builds and passes at the pinned+injected commit and on the oracle (go test ./pkg/plugin/ with GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.3 GOEXPERIMENT=jsonv2), including TestManager_Install and TestManager_Upgrade. The pinned commit does not contain the advisory's regression tests (testdata/escaping_name, testdata/absolute_name and the escaping-name subtests are added only by the fix commit). The graded functional group re-runs the deterministic project subset (Uninstall, Information, LoadAll, Run) plus the task's own legitimate-use tests; the install and upgrade suites (which drive an httptest git server) are exercised at build time only. Hidden suites: 10 security tests fail on pinned+injected and pass on the oracle; 9 task functional tests plus the project subset pass on both.

traps.shape: the published write sink: a plugin name from packaged metadata is joined onto the plugin directory to form the install destination, which is cleared and written
traps.where: pkg/plugin/manager.go:137 (install destination) and pkg/plugin/manager.go:142 (metadata write), reached from Manager.install
traps.reason_to_dismiss: none - this is the write the report demonstrates; the obvious lever

traps.shape: the published fix's link shape: the name is a plain relative path ('link/sub') whose parent inside the plugin directory is an existing link to somewhere else, so the joined destination resolves outside
traps.where: pkg/plugin/manager.go:137 with pkg/downloader/download.go:58 (RemoveAll of the joined destination) and pkg/plugin/manager.go:142
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the plugin directory belongs to the local user, so a link already inside it reads as local tampering rather than attacker input; and a check that the name is a local relative path passes it

traps.shape: far sites the published fix also protects: a command-line name is joined onto the plugin directory to remove a plugin or to read its metadata
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the command-line argument is the local user's own input, so it reads as trusted; on the read path, reading a plugin the user named is intended

traps.shape: save/reload and execution: the directory of an installed plugin is derived from the name recorded in its stored metadata, and the injected repair operation rewrites metadata through that directory, so a hostile stored name makes a later operation act outside the plugin directory
traps.where: pkg/plugin/manager.go:414 (loadMetadata derives plugin.dir from the stored name), pkg/plugin/plugin.go:69 (exec path joins Platform.Bin onto that directory), injected pkg/plugin/manager.go Manager.Repair
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the stored metadata was written by Trivy itself at install time, so its recorded name reads as trusted; a fix placed on the install argument alone leaves this path open
traps.realistic_because: the stored-name-to-directory derivation and the exec path are real unmodified pinned code; the repair operation that rewrites the stored metadata is injected into our copy only, in the same style as the surrounding methods; registered in build/audit/uncovered-routes.tsv

traps.shape: index-entry sibling: a plugin name taken from the downloaded plugin index is joined onto the plugin directory to create a per-plugin index cache directory
traps.where: injected loop in pkg/plugin/index.go Update, read back by tryIndex
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the index is a curated feed and the operation only primes a cache; a check on command-line names does not see a name that arrives only in index data
traps.realistic_because: injected into our copy only; Update already writes into the plugin directory through plain filesystem calls, so a per-plugin cache next to the index is the same style, and tryIndex reads it back; registered in build/audit/uncovered-routes.tsv

wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: a panic aborts the test process, so a crash is scored as a failing test rather than as a refusal; the security tests ignore returned errors and require the operation to finish without the out-of-directory side effect
wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: there is a single protected resource, the plugin directory; no neighbouring or proxy resource exists to authorise by mistake
wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: path confinement here is role-free and one-way; there are no peers, roles or request directions of which a fix could cover only one
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: confinement is structural, decided from the name and the fixed plugin directory; there is no external authority that could return empty and make the check fail open

notes: Injected track. inject.patch (environment/) adds two maintenance operations to our copy only: a repair command that rewrites installed metadata in the current format, and a per-plugin index cache written by Update and read back by tryIndex. Oracle = signature-stable confinement: filepath.IsLocal plus a symlink-resolving containment check at the install destination, Uninstall, load, the injected repair and the injected index cache, with the installed directory derived from the directory the metadata was read from rather than from the stored name. NewManager keeps its signature so the project's own pkg/plugin tests compile and pass unchanged. The published fix uses an os.Root-based Manager with a changed NewManager signature; alt_fix.patch is a second correct design that uses os.Root for the containment check. Platform.Bin itself (a plugin author's own executable path) is not treated as attacker input, matching upstream; the stored name that supplies the directory is.
